STEP 01
1
본문과 해석
본문 + 해석 + 핵심 어휘 정리
원문 PASSAGE
1The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess. 2Clear and perfect as it might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms. 3The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an "amorphous solid," for others a "supercooled liquid." 4In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter. 5In fact, at room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous one, even over long periods of time (though it can "sweat" if you don't add enough lime to the mix). 6Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking over time. 7Unless the church has endured temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances are they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and solidified in the first place. 8Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass. 9The paradox is that, despite it being one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does. 10Glass seems to obey most molecular laws. 11As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.
전체 해석
1유리의 구조는, 솔직히 말해서, 약간 엉망이다. 2우리 눈에는 맑고 완벽해 보일지 모르지만, 분자 수준에서 내려다보면, 유리는 원자들이 무작위로 뒤섞인 공 풀장처럼 보인다. 3이 엉망인 상태를 가리키는 전문 용어는 누구에게 묻느냐에 따라 다르다: 어떤 과학자들에게는 '무정형 고체'이고, 다른 이들에게는 '과냉각 액체'이다. 4이론적으로 유리는 액체이자 고체 모두이지만, 실제 거동 방식을 고려하면 실용적으로는 정말 후자(고체)에 가깝다. 5실제로, 실온에서 유리는 설령 감지할 수 없을 만큼 점성이 있는 액체라 하더라도, 오랜 시간에 걸쳐서도 액체처럼 행동하지 않는다(석회를 충분히 첨가하지 않으면 '땀을 흘릴' 수는 있지만). 6오래된 스테인드글라스 창문에서 가끔 볼 수 있는, 위보다 아래쪽이 더 두꺼운 변형된 유리 판들은, 유리가 시간이 지나면서 서서히 가라앉고 있기 때문에 그런 모양이 된 것이 일반적으로 아니다. 7그 교회가 400˚C 이상의 온도를 견뎌낸 것이 아닌 한, 그것들이 고르지 않은 이유는 애초에 그런 방식으로 불어서 굳혔기 때문일 가능성이 높다. 8판유리는 19세기에야 비로소 개발되었고, 우리는 진정으로 평평하고 얇은 유리판을 얻기 위해 20세기 중반까지 기다려야 했다. 9역설은, 유리가 가장 오래된 인간이 만든 물질 중 하나임에도 불구하고, 과학자들은 여전히 유리가 왜 그런 식으로 행동하는지 이해하려고 애쓴다는 것이다. 10유리는 대부분의 분자 법칙을 따르는 것처럼 보인다. 11한 유리 제조자가 말했듯이, 유리는 재료가 아니라 하나의 상태(state)이다.
필수 단어
1. frankly[부]솔직히 말해서
2. molecular[형]분자의
3. random[형]무작위의, 임의의
4. amorphous[형]무정형의, 형태가 없는
5. supercooled[형]과냉각된
6. imperceptibly[부]감지할 수 없을 만큼
7. viscous[형]점성이 있는, 끈적한
8. misshapen[형]모양이 뒤틀린, 변형된
9. stained-glass[형]스테인드글라스(채색 유리)의
10. endure[동]견디다, 참다
11. solidify[동]굳히다, 응고하다
12. uneven[형]고르지 않은, 불균일한
13. paradox[명]역설
14. substance[명]물질
15. comprehend[동]이해하다, 파악하다
16. struggle to[구]~하려고 애쓰다
17. obey[동]따르다, 복종하다
18. in the first place[구]애초에, 처음부터
19. given[전]~을 고려하면
20. despite[전]~에도 불구하고

STEP 01
1
본문과 해석
본문 + 해석 + 핵심 어휘 정리
동의어 ≈
1.frankly = honestly, candidly
2.molecular = atomic, microscopic
3.random = haphazard, arbitrary
4.amorphous = shapeless, unstructured
5.supercooled = undercooled
반의어 ↔
1.frankly ↔ evasively
2.molecular ↔ macroscopic
3.random ↔ ordered, systematic
4.amorphous ↔ crystalline, structured
5.supercooled ↔ —
영영풀이
1.amorphous: having no definite shape or form at the molecular level
2.paradox: something that contradicts itself or seems logically impossible yet is true
3.comprehend: to fully understand the meaning or nature of something
4.obey: to follow rules or commands without resistance
5.endure: to bear or withstand hardship or difficult conditions over time
필수 표현
1.despite: ~에도 불구하고
2.in theory: 이론적으로
3.in practice: 실제로, 실용적으로
4.in the first place: 애초에, 처음부터
5.given: ~을 고려하면

8.

Glass seems to obey most molecular laws.
11.

STEP 6 영문 배열 11문항
1
The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess.
2
Clear and perfect as it might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms.
3
The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an "amorphous solid," for others a "supercooled liquid."
4
In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter.
5
In fact, at room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous one, even over long periods of time (though it can "sweat" if you don't add enough lime to the mix).
6
Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes see in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking over time.
7
Unless the church has endured temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances are they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and solidified in the first place.
8
Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass.
9
The paradox is that, despite it being one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does.
10
Glass seems to obey most molecular laws.
11
As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.
